result.title: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
result.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a route to AI systems that participate in their own continued development. Recent methods allow language agents to retain changes to their parameters, memory, skills, and code for subsequent execution and improvement. We examine how these methods can inform new research ideas through two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce a unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions organized into four groups: update targets, update organization, update schedule and scope, feedback and selection. This taxonomy places existing methods in a shared design space, where examining individual dimensions and their interactions can inspire new research ideas. Second, we examine how existing RSI methods draw on traditional deep learning, for example through optimization, regularization, data augmentation, continual learning, and adversarial learning. We develop further ideas by examining more specific learning mechanisms and drawing on evolutionary computation. We also review how existing benchmarks assess self-improvement under online, offline, and offline-to-online settings. Together, these perspectives help researchers develop new RSI research ideas from existing designs and learning mechanisms. RSI papers and resources are available at https://prism-shadow.github.io/awesome-rsi/.

AI.brief_summary: 该文是一篇关于语言智能体「递归自我改进」（RSI）的综述/立场论文，提出涵盖更新目标、更新组织、更新调度与范围、反馈与选择四组九个维度的统一分类法，并梳理其与优化、正则化、持续学习、进化计算及在线/离线评测基准的联系，以启发新研究思路。
